question: In adults with overactive bladder or urge urinary incontinence, how do drug treatments compare with each other and with placebo in effectiveness and harms?
eligibility: Adults with overactive bladder, urge urinary incontinence or mixed urinary incontinence.
A drug for overactive bladder (for example oxybutynin, tolterodine, trospium, darifenacin, solifenacin, propiverine or flavoxate) compared with another drug, a different formulation or placebo.
Incontinence episodes, urinary frequency or urgency, quality of life, or adverse events.
Randomized controlled trials; controlled observational studies for harms.
as_of_source: Day after latest Entrez date among included SYNERGY records (lower bound).
source: Cohen et al. 2006 screening collection, UrinaryIncontinence SYNERGY subset (40 included PubMed IDs): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asreview/systematic-review-datasets/metadata-v1-final/datasets/Cohen_2006/output/online/UrinaryIncontinence.csv; source paper DOI https://doi.org/10.1197/jamia.M1929
notes: Question and eligibility reconstructed from the Drug Effectiveness Review Project (Oregon EPC) drug-class review this subset came from, not from its original protocol. The Cohen 2006 collection drew citations from a 1994-2003 MEDLINE subset (TREC 2004 Genomics), so gold covers 1994-2003 only: recall is valid, but result counts include earlier literature. The answer key uses label_included PubMed IDs (article-level inclusion).
